minutes.headline: Select Board appointed a Conservation Commission member; chapter 74 bylaw repeal left split 3-2 and carried to Feb. 13.
minutes.summary: The board heard extended public comment, appointed a new Conservation Commission member by roll call, and learned from the town manager that the town lost mid-year 40R smart growth aid. It reviewed ARPA fund balances and began a bylaw review, with a long debate on chapter 74 that ended without a vote. Members also discussed why a Proposition 2.5 override looks unlikely this year.

public_comment.topic: Complained about remarks at the Jan. 9 meeting, an assault, unplowed private roads, and responses from the police chief and town manager.
Thanked a DPW salt truck driver. Disappointed the town did not give Parks access to land at Lake Shirley, and that the budget does not reflect the value of education. Said she will not run in May.
Defended the town manager's 2.5% budget approach and opposed an override because of the burden on middle-class taxpayers.
Urged disbanding the elected Cemetery Commission and moving its funding to the DPW.
Urged the board to support hiring a grant writer in next year's budget.

votes.motion: Appoint Jenny puther to the Conservation Commission for a term expiring June 30, 2024
votes.outcome: passed (roll call; all members heard voting aye)
not audible (one member abstained, one said no; final count not stated)

budget_items.what_was_said: The town lost its mid-year 40R reimbursement because the calculation came out negative. The town manager does not plan to budget it next year.
The town manager recalled a large Chapter 70 increase last year, which moved the town from minimum aid to foundation aid, and said she would verify the figure.
The town manager said conservative local receipts estimates should cover the lost aid at year-end close.
Unspent committed ARPA balances were reviewed, and interest earned on the funds was noted.
Agreements are pending for the water district, the Boys and Girls Club and the food pantry.
A member described Westford using ARPA money for private well PFAS testing.
A consultant for solar on the old dump could be hired using available funding opportunities.
A speaker said the cemetery is funded annually through the DPW and that the commission requested capital funds.
Health insurance, Monty Tech and Worcester County Retirement numbers are still outstanding.
The finance committee voted to recommend a grant writer to the town manager and select board.

decisions.decision: The chair invited the state delegation and the school and finance committee chairs to meet on Feb. 20 about Prop 2.5 and 40R funding.
The town manager will schedule presentations from solar consultants and from Habitat for Humanity.
Chapter 74 repeal not voted; to be revisited Feb. 13, and the chapter 184 pawn broker bylaw was reviewed with no changes.
A business operating without a common victualler license is to appear before the board on Feb. 13.
The board will vote on the open space request after a site walk in mid-February, before the warrant closes.

what_happened.line: The Select Board appointed Jenny puther to the Conservation Commission by roll call, for a term expiring June 30, 2024.
The town manager reported the town lost its mid-year 40R smart growth reimbursement because the calculation came out negative, and does not plan to budget it next year.
The board debated the chapter 74 bylaw repeal at length and did not vote; it will return to the item on Feb. 13.
Members discussed FY25 budget inputs and an override; health insurance, Monty Tech and Worcester County Retirement numbers are still outstanding.
The chair invited the state delegation and the school and finance committee chairs to meet on Feb. 20 about Prop 2.5 and 40R funding.

why_it_matters: The lost 40R aid is a revenue shortfall the town manager expects local receipts to cover at year-end close, so it bears on how much room the FY25 budget has under the Proposition 2.5 levy limit.
With several FY25 cost inputs still outstanding and the override discussion unresolved, residents cannot yet tell whether a tax-bill question will reach a town vote this year.
The chapter 74 bylaw repeal is still undecided, so a bylaw change could come back for a vote on Feb. 13.
